You are l1_finding_agent in a multi-agent long-term memory pipeline.
Your operational type definition: stable observation, experiment result, comparison, failure mode, literature finding, data-quality finding, or evidence report.

Read only the bounded idea units below and propose only finding candidates.
Do not infer from outside this extraction scope.
Prior context may help disambiguate references, but it is never evidence.
Every candidate must be supported by the bounded idea units below.
The same idea unit may support other memory types; do not suppress valid finding objects for that reason.
Every candidate must set type exactly to finding.
Every candidate must include legacy_type using one of: argument, decision, method_change, open_question, result, todo. Use the closest old taxonomy role for comparison only.
Normally return 0-4 candidates. You may return up to 6 only
when there are clearly distinct durable finding memories. Return an empty list when
the batch has no durable finding. Do not pad the response to fill the limit.

Only output durable long-term memory:
- keep project-level decisions, method changes, concrete follow-ups, stable findings,
  unresolved research questions, or decision-supporting arguments
- do not restate each idea unit as a candidate
- do not output local clarifications, filler, examples, or one-line observations
- for argument, preserve only reasoning that explains a meaningful tradeoff or choice
- for open_question, preserve only questions that remain unresolved after the supplied scope
- for proposal, preserve only suggested options or hypotheses that are not yet adopted
- for action_item, preserve only executable follow-ups with a clear expectation of work
- for open_issue, preserve only unresolved issues that matter after this scope
- use importance >= 0.90 only for project-level or future-steering items
- use 0.50-0.70 for useful but local meeting-level context
Return JSON only. Text fields should prefer Traditional Chinese when the transcript is Chinese.

  [L1-0318-010] type=action_item quality=normal activity=active activation=0.86 reason=open_thread content=In the MEM 0 evaluation, the decision was made to compare performance against three baselines: feeding the full raw context to an LLM, using a RAG approach, and the benchmark results from the original LOCOMO paper.
  [L1-0318-009] type=decision quality=strong activity=active activation=0.93 reason=recent_high_importance content=For performance evaluation in MEM 0, the project decided to use an LLM-as-a-judge to provide a binary 'correct' or 'incorrect' assessment, thereby avoiding issues with semantic similarity metrics that can rate factually wrong answers highly.

  [L1-0307-015] type=open_issue quality=normal activity=fading activation=0.42 reason=open_thread content=The 'retrieve' phase of the memory system has not been designed. Bounded idea units:
U-S-0161-02-01 (174-177): The group is discussing how to evaluate the long-term memory claim of their three-layer architecture. They suggest a baseline without this architecture would just be fed the entire transcript, which they believe is not feasible for long texts.
U-S-0161-02-02 (178-179): A paper, possibly titled "HumanDigital", is mentioned as a reference for simulating human long-term memory. It was tested on general chatting history, and its applicability to their data format is questioned.
U-S-0161-02-03 (180-181): A specific evaluation strategy is proposed: use meetings 1 to N to build the memory, then use the (N+1)th meeting to evaluate by comparing the model's generated answers to the actual discussion. A simpler task is also mentioned: asking the model if a specific sentence was mentioned before.
U-S-0161-02-04 (182-185): The team has decided to use the ICSI corpus instead of their own recordings. The reason is that their own meetings lack strong coherence ("too spark"), while the ICSI corpus consists of a series of coherent, recorded research discussions.
U-S-0161-02-05 (186-186): After selecting the ICSI corpus, the team found little subsequent work using it for long-term memory in meetings; most usage is for speech annotation. They are now asking for suggestions on relevant data or methods.
